claims.statement: Under the full-Hermitian-domain premise and K=2Phi-I with K(I)=I, the factor-two EB existence problem is equivalent to the canonical support inequality S_d(Q) >= Tr_HS(QK) for every positive Hilbert-Schmidt operator Q. With a legal normalized symmetric extension Omega_RAB, this is Tr(Omega H_Q)-Tr_HS(Q) <= S_d(Q), where H_Q=sum_i w_i A_i^T tensor (A_i tensor I + I tensor A_i), Q=sum_i w_i |A_i><A_i|, and S_d(Q) is the density-matrix-measure moment support with barycenter I/d.
claims.status: internally derived exact finite-dimensional reduction; independently audited canonical compactness/domain caveats
assumptions: canonical POVM maps are compact and convex via density-matrix measures
claims.limits: This reduction is not a proof or a counterexample. H0-only feasibility does not force comparator unitality. General canonical maps are not equal to rank-one POVM maps, although rank-one refinement PSD-dominates and suffices for support/dominance.

claims.statement: For every 0<epsilon<1, an explicit canonical EB qubit channel with Bloch transfer diag(epsilon,0,1-epsilon) is admissible and has comparison constant 1, but admits no bistochastic CP map C with Phi=C* C.
claims.limits: Blocks the universal N92 bistochastic CP-square/Petz representation route only; it is not a factor-two EB counterexample.

claims.statement: A permutation-symmetric cubic-phase qutrit Choi extension yields a self-adjoint marginal Phi whose square is Hilbert-Schmidt-positive and remains self-compatible. A single 12-outcome four-MUB canonical EB map with traceless transfer I/4 dominates 2 Phi^2-I; exact top-space slack is (7-4 sqrt(3))/12>0.
claims.status: internally derived and exactly symbolically checked scoped control
claims.limits: This covers one nontrivial qutrit channel only and gives no uniform channel or dimension bound. The original cubic-phase marginal itself is not Hilbert-Schmidt-positive; the admissible example is its square.

claims.statement: For a selected six-mode d=5 Weyl dual with one real mode pair per projective line, an exact 25-dimensional Hermitian compression of the star operator has characteristic polynomial p(14)<0; hence lambda_max(H_Q)>14=Tr_HS(Q)+2 max_L |S intersect L|.
claims.status: exact algebraic proof of failure of a proposed line-PVM spectral shortcut
claims.limits: This does not violate the actual canonical support gate: S_5(Q) is a global POVM moment support, not the best one-line MUB score. The pure-state search is numerical and uncertified. No legal channel counterexample is supplied.

claims.statement: A finite two-qubit Pauli-invariant dual search found no positive candidate gap; sampled largest gap is approximately 3.7e-12.
claims.limits: Uses 180 sampled Q and 5,000 random pure states plus local ascent; support values are lower bounds, not global certificates. No theorem follows.

claims.statement: For odd-prime d and every Weyl-invariant positive dual Q on real traceless Hermitians, the star H_Q commutes with the simultaneous conjugate-Weyl/reference and Weyl/output action. Twirling any top eigenstate over displacements, phase-space parity, and output swap yields a positive normalized Choi state with all one-body marginals I/d, output symmetry, and the same star score; its induced marginal is unital, TP, CP, Weyl-covariant, and Hilbert-Schmidt-self-adjoint.

assumptions: Q is positive self-adjoint and Weyl-invariant
the full real mode-plane Weyl commutant is scalar on each plane
claims.limits: Parity forces real transfer coefficients but not nonnegative ones. The qubit covariant EB measure-prepare map with all Bloch transfers -1/3 is HS-self-adjoint and self-compatible but not HS-positive. Therefore the top-twirl is not automatically in the stricter target class requiring Phi>=0 as an HS operator.

claims.statement: For the selected six-mode d=5 Weyl-invariant Q from nonline_modes/D5_STAR_TWIRL_AND_SUPPORT.md, the top-twirled symmetric extension marginal is Hilbert-Schmidt-positive: all 24 nonidentity Weyl transfer coefficients exceed 0.472038.

claims.limits: This is a one-Q certificate, not an all-Q positivity theorem. The Q's actual support lower bound already exceeds the star target, so it is not a counterexample.

claims.statement: For d=5 and Q=(1/2)I_H0+(1/2)P_(1,0), the canonical pure-state moment support is exactly S_5(Q)=3; the exact star maximum is the unique root r in (15,16) of x^3-(31/2)x^2+(17/4)x+4, with Tr_HS(Q)=13. Hence every symmetric compatible extension satisfies 2 Tr_HS(Q Phi)-Tr_HS(Q)<=r-13<3=S_5(Q).

claims.statement: For an odd-prime Weyl-covariant, bistochastic, HS-self-adjoint, HS-positive, self-compatible channel with Weyl multipliers lambda_g in [0,1], if sum over projective lines L of r_L<=1, where r_L=max_{g in L}(2 lambda_g-1)_+, then one mixture of the line dephasing channels and depolarizing channel satisfies Psi >= 2 Phi-I on the full Hermitian space.
claims.status: internally derived exact scoped common-POVM theorem
claims.limits: The budget is sufficient only for this line-dephasing construction, not necessary for arbitrary EB maps. The exact d=5 compatible positive channel violates this budget but has a separate six-state EB comparator. No universal theorem follows.
